{'id': 0, 'text': 'Four reports from Counterpoint Research this week show that smartphone sales and shipments have declined in India, Latin America, Europe, and China. Below are the reports.'}

{'id': 1, 'text': 'Apple grew amid continued smartphone market decline'}

{'id': 2, 'text': 'While slowing smartphone sales and shipments are nothing new lately, four reports from Counterpoint Research this week make clear that memory shortages and rising prices are significantly impacting global demand.'}

{'id': 3, 'text': 'According to a report published yesterday, European smartphone shipments fell 10% year-over-year, hitting a three-year low.'}

{'id': 4, 'text': 'Even so, Apple grabbed nine percentage points of market share, tying with Samsung at 34% of shipments each. Chinese brands Xiaomi, Oppo, and Honor all lost share, ending the quarter at 15%, 4%, and 3% respectively.'}

{'id': 5, 'text': 'Turning to the Chinese smartphone market, Counterpoint\'s first 30 weeks of 2026 sales report noted that the market contracted 8.6% year-over-year, stating that "after the 618 shopping festival, the decline returned to double digits amid seasonal weakness and continued increases in memory costs."'}

{'id': 6, 'text': 'The firm added that Apple has entered a "seasonal slowdown" in July as it awaits the launch of its new iPhone lineup next month, while "some demand" was pulled forward around the 618 shopping festival.'}

{'id': 7, 'text': 'Another market with steep sales declines is India. Counterpoint data shows that following the end of a major online sales promotion in July, three consecutive weeks of year-over-year declines were recorded. During weeks 14 to 31, only two weeks saw year-over-year sales growth, and both coincided with major promotions.'}

{'id': 8, 'text': 'Counterpoint noted that sales during weeks 14 to 31 fell 14%, while Apple once again bucked the trend, posting 15% year-over-year growth, the "strongest sales growth during the period...primarily benefiting from continued demand for the iPhone 17 lineup, as well as ongoing installment offers."'}

{'id': 9, 'text': "Finally, Counterpoint's Q2 2026 Latin American smartphone shipments report published today indicated that the market fell 10% year-over-year, with only two major brands, Apple and Samsung, posting growth of 5% and 6% respectively."}

{'id': 10, 'text': 'The full reports follow:'}

{'id': 11, 'text': 'Counterpoint also noted that "Apple leads in Latin America\'s premium and high-end price tiers (>US$600) with about 51% share, while Samsung is the only sizable competitor, with about 40% share in that tier."'}

{'id': 12, 'text': "What are your thoughts on Apple's performance? Share them in the comments."}
